# A resistive divider

Two resistors set the output voltage. Read the signal path alongside each drawing.

## Schematic

<div class="beside" data-width="full" id="circuit">

1. The supply enters on the left and drives the first resistor.
2. The first resistor and the load form the two legs of a divider.
3. The output is the junction between those two legs. Measure it against ground.
4. If the resistor values match, the unloaded output is half the supply voltage.

<figure class="fig">
<h3>Signal path</h3>

```schematic
R1 in out 10k @0,0
R2 out 0 10k a@R1.b 0,74 v
VIN port in Input @-18,0
```

<figcaption>The signal falls across the two resistors.</figcaption>
</figure>
</div>

## Flowchart

<div class="beside" data-width="full" id="flow">

1. Start with the applied voltage and the resistance of each leg.
2. Divide the voltage by the total resistance to obtain the current.
3. Multiply the current by the resistance of the lower leg to obtain the output.
4. Check that the result lies between the supply voltage and ground.

<figure class="fig">
<h3>Calculation order</h3>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  input["Read the supply voltage"] --> current["Calculate the divider current"] --> output["Find the output voltage"]
```

<figcaption>Calculate the current before the output.</figcaption>
</figure>
</div>

## Image

<div class="beside" data-width="full" id="image">

1. The top of the strip is the supply end of the divider.
2. The marker halfway down is the unloaded output for equal resistors.
3. The bottom of the strip corresponds to ground.
4. A smaller lower resistor moves the output marker toward ground.

<figure class="fig">
<h3>Voltage scale</h3>
<img src={signal} alt="A vertical scale from supply through half voltage to ground" />
<figcaption>The image scales down to fit the pinned area.</figcaption>
</figure>
</div>
